title: The day of Arafah
hook: the pilgrims stand on the plain, and others fast the day

segments.voice: Yesterday: Eid, the feast at the end of Ramadan. Your line was a blessed feast. Did you say eid mubarak to anyone, even in a message? Day one hundred twenty-eight.

On the calendar, about two months and ten days pass after that first Eid. Then comes a day unlike any other in the Muslim year. Picture a wide, bare plain outside Mecca, a low hill in the middle of it, and the sun climbing. Two million people, sometimes more, dressed almost all alike in plain white. Nobody is shopping. Nobody is sightseeing. From noon until sunset, they mostly just stand there, and ask. And far away, in kitchens and offices on every continent, other Muslims skip breakfast that morning, because they're fasting the same day. Today: the day of Arafah.
screen: `A BARE PLAIN OUTSIDE MECCA.` → `MILLIONS IN WHITE, STANDING.` → `AND FAR AWAY, A FAST.`

segments.voice: Arafah is the ninth day of Dhu al-Hijjah, the month of the pilgrimage, and it's also the name of the plain itself. The Hajj has many rites: circling the Kaaba, walking between two hills, throwing pebbles, the sacrifice. But the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, peace be upon him, summed it up in two words, reported by Tirmidhi and Abu Dawud: the Hajj is Arafah. Miss the standing on that plain, and in the view of the scholars, you've missed the Hajj. The standing is called wuquf. There's no fixed script for it. People pray, recite, weep, ask for forgiveness, ask for their families, in Arabic and in every other language. Tirmidhi reports that the best supplication is the supplication of the day of Arafah. Sahih Muslim adds that there's no day on which Allah frees more people from the Fire. It's a day of history too. The Prophet gave his farewell sermon on this plain, on his only Hajj, a few months before he died. And Bukhari reports that one line of the Qur'an came down on a Friday at Arafah: This day have I perfected your religion for you. Now the other half of the picture. Most Muslims will never stand at Arafah, or will stand there once. So for everyone at home, the tradition offers the fast. Sahih Muslim reports that fasting the day of Arafah is hoped to wipe away the sins of the year before and the year after. The pilgrims usually don't fast; they need their strength to stand. Everyone else does. One day, two ways of keeping it: standing on the plain, or fasting at your desk.
screen: `THE NINTH DAY, AND THE PLAIN.` · `THE HAJJ IS ARAFAH.` · `A FAREWELL, AND A FINISHED VERSE.` · `AT HOME: THE FAST.` · then, large: `ONE DAY, TWO WAYS TO KEEP IT.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: give one day's worth of focus. Sit or stand, whichever feels more like the plain. Picture the whole of today, from waking to sleep, as one long afternoon of standing. Now choose one thing you'll give your full attention to today, and only one: a person, a piece of work, a question you keep avoiding. Hold it in mind. If you pray, you can ask for help with it, in any words you have. If not, simply stay with it and let everything else wait. The bell holds the time.
Arafah. The ninth day of the pilgrimage month, and the plain where the pilgrims stand from noon to sunset. Today's word.

Your line: the standing day. Somewhere in today, when you'd normally reach for your phone, stand still for one minute instead, and ask for one thing, or simply notice where you are. Day one hundred twenty-eight.

howItsDone: On the ninth of Dhu al-Hijjah, pilgrims stand on the plain of Arafah from midday to sunset in prayer and supplication, while many Muslims who are not on Hajj fast that day.
